copies.headline: Tight end gap buries the champ
copies.body:
Adam lost this at tight end, and it wasn't close. Trey McBride went for 27.1 while Sam LaPorta managed 2.8 on a 12.7 projection — a 24.3-point hole in one lineup slot, which is almost exactly the final margin. Everything else was a wash or worse: Caleb Williams outscored Brock Purdy by 10.1, Brock Bowers in the flex beat Jalen Coker by 11.4, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 31.3 only got Adam back to even on the week.
The flex was self-inflicted. Coker scored 1.9 on a 15.4 projection with Rico Dowdle (14.6) and Rome Odunze (10.9) sitting behind him. Kenneth Walker III chipping in 9.7 on a 19.1 projection didn't help. Adam's 103.0 is his season low by 29.7 points, and he still leads the league at 144.0 per game, which tells you how high the bar normally sits.
Adam drops to 6-1 but owns an 81 percent all-play — nobody's panicking. John climbs to 4-3 with the league's second-best scoring and an all-play that says he should be better than that. We had him by nine. He took 24.7 instead.

copies.headline: Likely and the Chiefs Sink Logan Again
copies.body:
Joe Burrow went for 28.9 and Logan still lost, which tells you everything about where this one came apart. Isaiah Likely put up 3.2 against a 14.3 projection, and the Chiefs D/ST went negative at minus-1.0. That's a 19.3-point hole at two spots Isaac won by 10.3 and 9.0 — more than enough to swallow Logan's 12.4-point quarterback edge. Justin Jefferson chipping in 8.4 on an 18.5 projection out of the flex didn't help.
Isaac won by being boring. Javonte Williams 21.5, Malik Nabers 18.1, Ja'Marr Chase 17.2, nobody disastrous. The bench stings — Bo Nix scored 26.2 while C.J. Stroud managed 16.5, and Cam Skattebo's 19.1 sat behind J.K. Dobbins' 8.3 — but you don't get to complain about process when the margin is 7.6. We picked Logan by 14, which was defensible right up until Likely caught nothing.
Logan is 2-5 with 119.0 points per game, fifth in the league, and an all-play mark of 44-33. He's two full wins below expectation. Isaac is 3-4 at 103.6 a week and 25-52 on all-play, the 11th-best scorer in a 12-team league. One of these men is cursed and it isn't the one who won.

copies.headline: Pollard and Judkins Bury the Aura Farm
copies.body:
Running backs decided this before anyone touched a ball in the second half. Grant got 59.9 from Tony Pollard and Quinshon Judkins — Pollard alone outscored Christian's entire backfield three times over — against 13.4 from Chase Brown and Aaron Jones Sr. That's a 46.5-point hole, and a 36.3-point final means every other position essentially canceled out. Christian actually won QB, TE, kicker and defense, including nine free points from a Jets unit that posted a zero, and it didn't matter at all.
The misses compound. Aaron Jones went for 3.6 on a 12.3 projection while Alvin Kamara put up 13.2 on the bench, a swap that still loses but makes it respectable. Pat Freiermuth chipping in 4.0 at flex didn't help. CeeDee Lamb and Jameson Williams combined for 50.5 and got nothing for it.
Christian is 2-5 with the third-best scoring and a 46-31 all-play — he's 2.2 wins light. We picked him by seven. Grant, meanwhile, is 4-3 on a season-high 158.6 and still eighth in the power rankings, which is the Grant experience in one sentence.

copies.headline: Tight End Gap Buries CJ By Two
copies.body:
Two points, and you can trace all of them to tight end. Kyle Pitts put up 13.2 for Leif; Juwan Johnson managed 1.7 for CJ, an 11.5-point hole in the one spot where CJ had no answer. CJ won the backfield by 14 behind Jonathan Taylor's 19.0 and took the D/ST 9-0 when the Texans posted a donut, and it still wasn't enough, because Kirk Cousins outscored Tyler Shough by 6.6 and Christian McCaffrey's 22.0 beat anything CJ put in flex.
The real killer was the receiver room. Ted Hurst III started and scored zero on a 10.0 projection while Devaughn Vele's 16.4 sat on the bench, and Emanuel Wilson's 18.5 rotted behind Chuba Hubbard's 10.0. Any one of those swaps flips this. DK Metcalf chipping in 7.6 on 14.8 just made it worse.
We had CJ by 11, which aged terribly. He's 4-3 with his worst output of the season; Leif is 5-2 on three straight wins he's mostly earned, and the rivalry stays knotted at 4-4.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Skill Positions Vanish, Kaleb Cruises
copies.body:
The game was decided in the flex and the back half of Mitchell's lineup. Kaleb got 21.3 from Tre Tucker and 35.6 from his backfield; Mitchell countered with Jordan Mason at 6.8 and Roschon Johnson at 1.3 on a 9.1 projection, which is the kind of start that loses games before the receivers even touch the ball. Then Nico Collins — the guy the team is literally named after — put up 2.6 on a 16.7 projection. Even Jahmyr Gibbs missed by 8.7. Four starters combined for 14 points.
Kaleb didn't need to be great, and wasn't exactly: Harrison Butker gave him 3.0 and KC Concepcion dropped 23.2 on the bench while Carnell Tate managed 9.9. He still won by 52.1.
We picked Mitchell by nine, which aged about as well as the Collins start. Kaleb is 5-2 with an all-play of 34-43 and nearly two wins of luck banked — the 2023 Cinderella getting away with it again. Mitchell is 1-6 and no longer a coin flip.

copies.headline: Peter's Receivers Bail Out A Dead Quarterback
copies.body:
This was decided at wide receiver, where Peter got 34.6 to Noah's 15.2 and banked a 19.4-point cushion he needed every inch of. Tee Higgins went for 26.8, George Pickens added 15.7 from the flex, and that was enough to survive J.J. McCarthy's 10.2 (6.2 under projection), A.J. Brown's 7.8 on a 15.9 number, and a kicker-plus-defense combination that produced two total points. Two. Peter won a game in which half his lineup no-showed.
Noah had the quarterback edge — Drake Maye 27.4 against McCarthy's 10.2 — and still lost by 6.6, because Garrett Wilson gave him 4.6 on a 15.1 projection and Hunter Henry sat on the bench with 14.1 while Jaylen Waddle started for 8.8. That swap alone covers the margin twice over. Our preview had Peter by 12, which was close enough.
Noah falls to 1-6 with a 24-53 all-play, which is less bad luck than it is the worst scoring in the league. But he's the 7-seed guy with five playoff wins, so nobody's relaxed. Peter's 5-2 with a +2.0 luck rating — the 2022 version of him didn't need the help.

intro: Leif survived CJ by two points, which is less a win than a clerical error, and Peter's 114.58 over Noah was the only other game inside a touchdown. Everything else was a formality: Grant hung 158.6 on Christian, Kaleb buried Mitchell by 52 while Mitchell's 79.38 set the week's floor, and John cleared Adam by 24.7 without ever looking stressed. Six games, two of them competitive, and Mitchell scoring 79 points at home is going to follow him around for a while.
